slides.title: LF AI & Data Foundation Welcomes AIRSEAI to Unite Open Source Embodied AI Ecosystem
slides.highlight: The addition of AIRSEAI to the LF AI & Data Foundation supports the development of an open source embodied AI ecosystem, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: RoboColiseum Launches Standardized Simulation Platform for Embodied AI Evaluation
slides.tldr: STANDARDIZED SIMULATION PLATFORM FOR EMBODIED AI
slides.highlight: The launch of a standardized simulation platform for embodied AI evaluation is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated embodied learning.

slides.title: TurnBench: A Multi-Domain Benchmark for Turn-Taking Dynamics in Spoken Dialogue
slides.highlight: TurnBench provides a hand-labeled corpus and evaluation protocol for end-of-turn and interruption detection, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: TurnBench is a multi-domain benchmark for evaluating end-of-turn and interruption detection in spoken dialogue.
card.key_idea: A 30-hour triple-annotated corpus across six interaction styles with a standardized evaluation protocol to measure recall, false positive rate, and latency for turn-taking systems.
card.evaluation: 14 heterogeneous systems were tested; VAP performed best. Results show interruption false positives are highly dependent on conversation type, particularly in backchannel-dense styles.
card.limitation: The dataset is limited to English, dyadic, studio-recorded conversations and lacks a methodology for evaluating interruptions in full-duplex models.

slides.title: LLM-Based Selection of Incongruent Verbal and Nonverbal Behavior for Virtual Humans
slides.highlight: This work explores using LLMs to select mismatched verbal and nonverbal behaviors based on social context, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: LLMs can generate realistic virtual human behaviors where nonverbal cues contradict verbal content based on context.
card.key_idea: A taxonomy of verbal-nonverbal mismatches (e.g., irony, deception) was used to test three prompting levels: utterance-only, dialogue history, and dialogue plus explicit situational context.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via Claude-3.5-Sonnet output analysis and two human-subject studies (N=49 and N=39) using video stimuli and Likert scales; results were statistically significant.
card.limitation: The study excluded gestures, postural shifts, and voice prosody, and requires manual mapping of LLM descriptions to animation parameters.

slides.title: Generative Action-Chunk Sampling for Adaptive Stiffness Control in Physical Human-Robot Collaboration
slides.tldr: ADAPTIVE STIFFNESS CONTROL VIA GENERATIVE SAMPLING
slides.highlight: This research proposes a framework that uses variation in sampled action chunks to adapt robot stiffness, balancing assistance and compliance during physical human-robot interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied AI.

card.one_liner: Adaptive robot stiffness control using variation among sampled generative action chunks for physical human-robot collaboration.
card.key_idea: A CVAE-based policy samples multiple action chunks from an observation-conditioned prior; high sample variation triggers lower stiffness for compliance, while low variation increases stiffness for assistance.
card.evaluation: Real-world collaborative transport task (4 directions). Proposed method achieved 0.95 success rate, outperforming fixed-stiffness ablation (0.83) and deterministic FACTR (0.69).
card.limitation: The action-deviation signal is a proxy for uncertainty, not a calibrated probability of human intention or epistemic uncertainty.

slides.title: Pose-Anchored Optical Flow for Low-Latency Human Action Anticipation in Human-Robot Teaming
slides.highlight: PoseOFF uses pose-anchored optical flow to capture local motion around joints, enabling earlier human intent understanding for more responsive human-robot interaction. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: PoseOFF improves early human action anticipation by anchoring local optical flow features to skeleton joints.
card.key_idea: It extracts local optical flow windows around human keypoints and integrates these motion features into skeleton-based models via a lightweight CNN embedding layer.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on NTU RGB+D 60/120 and UCF101 using InfoGCN++, MS-G3D, and ST-GCN++. Results show higher accuracy at early observation ratios and improved AUC.
card.limitation: Less effective under severe occlusion or for actions dominated by large-scale global motion patterns.

slides.authors: Lewis de Zoete Grundy et al.

slides.title: Beyond Local Surprise: Grounded Dialogue as Selective Belief Revision under Referential Uncertainty
slides.tldr: DIALOGUE BELIEF REVISION UNDER REFERENTIAL UNCERTAINTY
slides.highlight: This research explores how listeners decide to preserve or revise their understanding during dialogue, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and social perception.

card.one_liner: Successful grounded dialogue relies on uncertainty-sensitive revision rather than reacting to local linguistic mismatch.
card.key_idea: A framework comparing four revision policies for updating visual grounding; it finds that preserving interpretations despite local mismatch and revising based on accumulated uncertainty optimizes coherence.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on PhotoChat using visual retrieval (R@K, MRR) and intrinsic dynamics. Results show uncertainty-sensitive policies outperform surprise-driven ones in retrieval stability.
card.limitation: Evaluated on a single dataset (PhotoChat) with cooperative interactions, potentially favoring persistence-based strategies over more unstable communicative settings.

slides.title: Free-Energy-Gated Plasticity for Real-Time Online Motor Learning in Physical Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: REAL-TIME ONLINE MOTOR LEARNING VIA FREE-ENERGY-GATED PLASTICITY
slides.highlight: This work introduces Free-Energy-Gated Plasticity (FEGP) to enable robots to acquire and retain motor patterns during real-time physical interaction, supporting RwB's focus on embodied learning and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: FEGP enables robots to learn multiple motor patterns online without forgetting, using free energy to regulate plasticity.
card.key_idea: A sigmoidal plasticity gate scales synaptic updates based on variational free energy, increasing learning during model-environment mismatch and suppressing it when predictions are accurate.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 10 randomized teaching streams and physical human-robot interaction. Metrics included repertoire coverage, retention, and DTW shape distance; results showed significant improvement over constant rates.
card.limitation: The method relies on a sliding window of recent observations, which may limit long-term memory without further architectural extensions.

slides.title: AffectSim: A Controllable Interactive 3D Simulation Benchmark for Embodied Affective Perception
slides.tldr: INTERACTIVE 3D BENCHMARK FOR EMBODIED AFFECTIVE PERCEPTION
slides.highlight: AffectSim provides a controllable 3D simulation to study how agent viewpoint and sensing influence emotion perception, supporting the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: AffectSim is a 3D simulation benchmark for studying how embodied agent movement improves affective perception.
card.key_idea: It decouples affective human motions from 3D scene observation conditions, allowing the same emotion-labeled behavior to be re-observed under varied distances, orientations, and occlusions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 24 frozen perception models across 27,647 episodes. A two-stage active-observation baseline improved 21/24 configurations, recovering up to 32% of the observation-quality gap.
card.limitation: The benchmark currently uses cyclically replayed motions, factoring out event-timing uncertainty and temporally evolving behaviors.

slides.title: Why Personalization Matters: Cross-Subject Challenges in EMG-IMU-based HRI Activity Recognition
slides.tldr: PERSONALIZATION IN EMG-IMU ACTIVITY RECOGNITION FOR HRI
slides.highlight: This research introduces the MAGIC-HRI dataset and demonstrates that personalization is necessary to overcome subject dependence in wearable-based activity recognition for human-robot interaction, supporting the RwB goal of improving embodied social robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Personalization is essential for robust EMG-IMU activity recognition in HRI due to high inter-subject variability.
card.key_idea: Introduces MAGIC-HRI dataset (53 classes) using Random Forest classifiers, demonstrating that injecting few subject-specific samples significantly improves Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) generalization performance.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 11 participants using accuracy and F1-score. Random Forest was the strongest baseline; LOSO revealed a 60% performance gap versus standard splits.
card.limitation: Lacks robot-in-the-loop evaluation in online settings and shows poor initial generalization to unseen users without personalization.

slides.authors: Ruan Rithelle Chagas de Faria Carminati et al.

slides.title: Counterfactual Explanations and the Scope of Contestability
slides.tldr: ENHANCING ALGORITHMIC CONTESTABILITY VIA COUNTERFACTUAL EXPLANATIONS
slides.highlight: This research explores how counterfactual explanations can reinstate human agency and facilitate the contestability of algorithmic decisions in societal domains, aligning with MIMIC's focus on the impact analysis of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: The paper examines if counterfactual explanations enable users to effectively contest opaque algorithmic decisions.
card.key_idea: Defines contestability as providing sufficient information to revoke decisions and proposes a multi-shot counterfactual querying approach to better detect algorithmic errors.

slides.authors: Alice C. W. Huang et al.

slides.title: Counterfactual, Per-Decision Bias Auditing for Automated Hiring: Localizing and Explaining Disparate Impact in Applicant Tracking Systems
slides.tldr: PER-DECISION BIAS AUDITING FOR HIRING SYSTEMS
slides.highlight: The AI Bias Firewall (AIBF) provides a method for localizing and explaining disparate impact in automated hiring, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale impact analysis of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: AIBF audits automated hiring by using counterfactual shifts to localize and explain individual biased decisions.
card.key_idea: It neutralizes protected-attribute proxies to a privileged baseline, measures the resulting score shift, and uses additive attribution for plain-language explanations of the bias.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Adult and COMPAS datasets; achieved 0.963 AUC for detecting flips and surfaced 55% of harmed candidates by reviewing only 5% of decisions.
card.limitation: Correcting flagged decisions improves but doesn't reach legal parity because merit features often contain residual proxy correlations.

slides.title: AgentConnect Introduces Open-Source Multi-Agent Collaboration
slides.highlight: AgentConnect provides open-source multi-agent collaboration, which is relevant to MIMIC's focus on agent models for societal-scale simulation.

slides.title: Simulating Cognitive Smart Freight Corridors with Agent-Based Models and Reinforcement Learning
slides.tldr: AGENT-BASED MODELING FOR SMART FREIGHT CORRIDORS
slides.highlight: This work utilizes agent-based modeling and multi-agent reinforcement learning to simulate adaptive vehicle behaviors, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: An ABM framework using RL and MARL to optimize platoon formation and charging in smart freight corridors.
card.key_idea: A three-layer architecture (physical, cyber, decision) coupling a Python-based ABM with a DQN corridor controller and MARL station agents for adaptive traffic and energy management.
card.evaluation: Compared Baseline, Assisted, and Cognitive scenarios using throughput, congestion, and energy metrics. Results show Cognitive scenario increases throughput by 27% and reduces congestion by 63.9%.
card.limitation: The model uses a unidirectional network and lacks empirical validation with real freight demand data or established optimization benchmarks.
